| **Relay routing** | Not a new D3 exception — reuse the existing relay-hint plumbing that `nevent`/`naddr` already use (hints used once, never merged into the outbox/gossip model). | [...] - Relay pinning for an arbitrary filter: `InterestShape.relay_pin` (`crates/nmp-planner/src/interest/shape.rs:99-126`) → planner Case E (`compiler/partition::case_e_relay_pinned`), works for any shape and any lifecycle, never serialized to wire, refuses merge (lattice Rule 9). N relays = N pinned demands — exactly how NIP-50 search does it today (`crates/nmp-nip50/src/search/session.rs:225-236`).
- The #1563 finding holds: `build_interest_pair` (`crates/nmp-core/src/subs/interest_builder.rs`) parses arbitrary NIP-01 filter JSON. "Arbitrary filter" was never the gap. [...] ## Q4. One-shot relay invariant — YES, existing precedent, no new D3 exception

Two shipped precedents, both "used once, never persisted to NIP-65/gossip":
- `relay_hints` (`crates/nmp-core/src/kernel/requests/event.rs:128-140`) — the one-shot single-event claim variant #2948 cites. Correct in spirit, wrong vehicle for a filter (Case-D-only, see Q2 caveat).
- `InterestShape.relay_pin` — the stronger, already-generic vehicle: client-side routing only, never serialized onto the wire, merge-refused (Rule 9, `planner/src/lattice/rules.rs:161`), used in production by NIP-29 hosts and NIP-50 pinned search. AD rides this. Nothing new to invent or except.
